expectations.text: Presents 2-3 candidate designs ordered by efficiency with one recommended, and waits for the user's pick rather than delivering a single final design.
expectations.evidence: Section 2 presents three designs (A, B, C) labelled 'ordered by efficiency' and recommends B with a reason. That half of the item is met. The other half is not. The transcript says 'Your pick is needed before section 3 onward is final', yet the rest of the charter assumes B and works it out in full: blueprint, build plan, integrity, renewal, pricing, operating model, kill rule and CEO talking points. It also saves the charter to memory. Asking the user to 'pick A or B' only at the very end is not waiting for the pick, because a complete single design was already delivered.
